# GarminFood

A personal iOS food-tracking app — fast logging, a streak, levels, challenges, a real design system — with Garmin Connect as the system of record, since no public Garmin API exists for writing nutrition data. Built against Garmin's private mobile API, on a free Apple developer account, with no Mac.

**This repository is a plan plus a working build pipeline, not a finished app yet.** Everything lives under `openspec/` as seven ordered OpenSpec changes, and `ios/` holds the actual Xcode project (generated by XcodeGen, built by GitHub Actions).

## Read this first

- [`openspec/config.yaml`](openspec/config.yaml) — project context, hard constraints, Design & UX principles, and everything established by live-probing the owner's Garmin account and real-device testing on 2026-09-14.
- **No paid Apple Developer Program.** Ships on a free Personal Team, built in CI (GitHub Actions macOS runners — free and unlimited on this public repo), signed and installed locally via AltServer + AltStore.
- **Confirmed by a real device test: there is no shared state at all between the app and its widget/Control extensions** — no App Group, no Keychain Sharing (`errSecMissingEntitlement`/-34018). This has two concrete consequences, both already worked into the plan:
  - Widgets **cannot show live data, ever** — not Garmin data, not local app data. They are static "tap to open the app" shortcuts (Home Screen and Lock Screen both work fine for this).
  - A Control's logging action must briefly open the app to reach its stored Garmin login, rather than running fully invisibly.

## The seven changes, in order

1. **[`establish-garmin-nutrition-contract`](openspec/changes/establish-garmin-nutrition-contract/)** — read-only recon. Confirmed the nutrition API is live and found the food-log write route by decompiling the Garmin Android client. **Done.**
2. **[`add-garmin-auth-and-sync`](openspec/changes/add-garmin-auth-and-sync/)** — browser-based token bootstrap, independent per-process credential bootstrap (no cross-process sharing exists), and a per-process durable outbox with reconciliation against Garmin. The Mac-less build → sign → install loop (tasks 6.1–6.4) is built and verified end to end; OAuth1 Swift port (task group 7) is next.
3. **[`add-food-log-core`](openspec/changes/add-food-log-core/)** — the food catalog (search, favourites, barcode scanning — deprioritized, poor Czech coverage — and custom foods) and the confirm-and-log flow.
4. **[`add-gamification`](openspec/changes/add-gamification/)** — a streak (with a one-miss-per-week grace), levels/XP, and rotating challenges, all computed locally from the log history. The engagement layer that makes daily logging worth doing.
5. **[`add-glanceable-surfaces`](openspec/changes/add-glanceable-surfaces/)** — Controls for Control Center/Lock Screen/Action Button (brief app-open per tap, not invisible — see above), and static open-the-app widgets for Home Screen and Lock Screen. No Live Activity (its 8h/12h cap can't hold a 24h total) and no live-updating widget (structurally impossible on this account).
6. **[`add-companion-surfaces`](openspec/changes/add-companion-surfaces/)** — fixed the existing Obsidian vault's `sync-nutrition.mjs`, which had silently called a dead route since it was written. **Done**, pending the owner's own commit review in that separate repo.
7. **[`add-czech-food-catalog`](openspec/changes/add-czech-food-catalog/)** — a second, Czech-focused food search source (Open Food Facts, openly licensed, with genuine local coverage Garmin's own FatSecret-backed database lacks), shown as a visibly separate catalog section; logging a Czech-database food matches it against Garmin's own catalog first, and only falls back to creating a new food in Garmin (`createCustomFood`, gated behind an explicit user confirmation, request body unconfirmed) when no equivalent exists.
8. **[`add-meal-presets`](openspec/changes/add-meal-presets/)** — save a named, multi-ingredient meal once (each ingredient a real catalog/Czech-database food or an existing custom food) and log the whole thing in one action: one outbox entry per ingredient, sharing meal type/date, built entirely on the existing single-food confirm path rather than a new, unconfirmed aggregated-Garmin-food write.
9. **[`add-reminders-and-diagnostics`](openspec/changes/add-reminders-and-diagnostics/)** — configurable local reminders (meals, streak-at-risk, daily challenges) that only fire when their condition still holds, plus a persistent in-app diagnostics log (Garmin API/outbox failures, confirm-screen errors) that's viewable and copyable entirely on-device — no Mac needed to see what actually went wrong.

Changes 3–6 all depend on 1 and 2; 4, 5 and 6 can proceed in parallel once 3 exists. Change 7 depends on 2 and 3. Change 8 depends on 3. Change 9 depends on 3 and 4.

## What's actually built and verified right now

- `ios/` — an XcodeGen-generated Xcode project (app + widget extension), building green in CI.
- `.github/workflows/build.yml` — builds for Simulator, archives unsigned for device, uploads the `.ipa` as an artifact. Never signs anything; that happens locally via AltServer/AltStore with the owner's own Apple ID.
- The full loop — CI build → AltServer sign → AltStore install → app runs on a real iPhone — is confirmed working, not just assumed.
- The home screen was redesigned around a streak + calorie hero rather than a progress ring (`ios/GarminFood/Home/TodayHeroView.swift`, `HomeView.swift`, `MomentOverlay.swift`) — a big calorie number and the streak flame are the two things the app leads with, with `MomentOverlay` handling level-up/streak-milestone celebration on top rather than a separate screen.
- The Czech (Open Food Facts) food catalog (`add-czech-food-catalog`) is implemented: `FoodLogCore/OpenFoodFactsClient.swift` searches OFF's legacy free-text endpoint and decodes results into the same `Food`/`Serving` shape Garmin results use; `FoodLogCore/GarminFoodMatching.swift` is the pure name/calorie matching heuristic (unit-tested); `GarminFood/Catalog/MatchConfirmationView.swift` shows the match (or lack of one) and the gated "Create in Garmin" fallback, which is the only call site of `GarminKit`'s new (request-body-unconfirmed) `GarminClient.createCustomFood`. None of this has been exercised against the real OFF API or a real Garmin write yet — it's built and unit-tested, not live-verified.
- The Keychain-sharing spike (`ios/Shared/KeychainSpike.swift`, `ios/GarminFoodWidget/KeychainCheckWidget.swift`) produced the definitive negative result above; both were throwaway test code, since removed now that the real app doesn't need them.
- Meal presets (`add-meal-presets`) are implemented: `FoodLogCore/MealPreset.swift` (a named group of ingredient snapshots) and `LogEntryCoordinator.confirmMealPreset` (one outbox entry per ingredient, built on the existing single-food confirm path — no new, unconfirmed Garmin write), plus `GarminFood/MealPreset/` (editor + confirm screens) and entry points from `FoodCatalogView`'s "Your meals" section and `TodayView`'s "Log a meal" shelf. Unit-tested; not yet exercised on a real device.
- Reminders and diagnostics (`add-reminders-and-diagnostics`) are implemented: configurable local reminders (`NotificationPlanning.swift`, `NotificationScheduler.swift`) for meals/streak/daily-challenges, each self-cancelling once its condition no longer holds, and a persistent, in-app, copyable diagnostics log (`GarminKit/DiagnosticsLog.swift`) fed from `GarminClient`, `Outbox.drain`, and confirm-screen error paths — both reachable from Settings. Neither needs a paid Apple Developer account. Unit-tested (the pure planning logic); not yet exercised on a real device.

## What remains genuinely unverified

- The browser-based Garmin sign-in flow (`GarminAuthSession.swift`) — the exact SSO sign-in URL, whether a custom URL scheme redirect works at all, and the ticket→OAuth1 exchange shape are all inferred, not observed working (see that file's own header).
- The first real Garmin food-log write (`createFoodLogEntry`) and the new `createCustomFood` write this change adds — both are documented-but-unconfirmed request contracts; failures surface loudly to the user rather than silently, by design.
- Any visual/UX QA on a real device — everything SwiftUI-side has been authored and reasoned about without a local Xcode/Simulator to actually look at it (no Mac; see above).

## Tools (read-only, already run against the live Garmin account)

- `tools/lib/garmin-auth.mjs` — OAuth1→OAuth2 exchange, lifted from the vault's working Node client.
- `tools/probe-garmin-nutrition.mjs` — reads its route list from `docs/garmin-routes.json` and reports Gate 0 status.
- `tools/discover-nutrition-routes.mjs` — wide route/parameter sweep; this is how `searchExpression` and `barCode` were found.
- `tools/garmin-get.mjs` — ad hoc authenticated GET against any path.

All four are GET-only. Run them with `VAULT_ROOT` pointed at the Obsidian vault holding the Garmin tokens:

```
VAULT_ROOT="/path/to/vault" node tools/garmin-get.mjs '/nutrition-service/food/search?searchExpression=banana'
```

See [`docs/garmin-routes.json`](docs/garmin-routes.json) for the full route registry and [`docs/garmin-food-log-contract.md`](docs/garmin-food-log-contract.md) for the write contract.

## Validating the plan

```
npm install -g @fission-ai/openspec
openspec validate --all --strict
```
